subject: P0: BlueCove throughput collapse in us-west2 — cross-region drain & exec action
messages:
From: Charlie Nguyen <charlie@bluecove.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@bluecove.com>, BlueCove SRE <sre@bluecove.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production alert: sustained 5xx + token latency spike in us-west2

Rafael —

We're seeing a sustained throughput collapse for our read-heavy checkout flows hitting your us-west2 AZs starting ~07:55 PT. Error rates moved from ~0.5% to 18% and p95 token latency jumped from ~120ms to 2.8s. The customer-facing checkout errors are now impacting ~12% of sessions.

Attached a small sample of logs and request traces (request-logs.zip). Key observations:
- Amplified 502s originating from Redwood gateway in us-west2 cluster A
- KV cache hit-rate dropped sharply for prefetched prefixes
- Traffic spike correlates to a BlueCove marketing batch (we can provide the campaign id)

We need immediate help routing or mitigation. Can you open an incident bridge and tell us what temporary mitigations you can put in place? SLA impact is material.

— Charlie
SRE Lead, BlueCove Retail

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Charlie Nguyen <charlie@bluecove.com>, Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@bluecove.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production alert: sustained 5xx + token latency spike in us-west2

Thanks for the rapid flag, Charlie — I’m on it. Opening an incident bridge now (see internal link below).

Short plan (need confirmations):
1) Immediate: enable cross-region drain for BlueCove from us-west2 -> us-east1 (start with 10% canary) to shed pressure on problematic AZs.
2) Simultaneous: pin BlueCove traffic to the lower-latency quantized variant in us-west2 for read flows (reduces token compute).
3) Ops: refill KV caches for the prefixes flagged in sample logs; apply aggressive negative cache TTLs where safe.
4) Customer comms: provide timeline and expected RTO <= 30m for canary, 90m for full switch.

Vanessa/Hannah/David — can you confirm capacity in us-east1 for a 20% immediate bump, and whether we need leadership sign-off to override regional routing guardrails? I will coordinate exec-level comms to Lisa once we have the mitigation path.

Attachment: incident-3765-snapshot.png (snapshot of metric spikes).

Rafael Mendes
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Charlie Nguyen <charlie@bluecove.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 08:29:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production alert: sustained 5xx + token latency spike in us-west2

Rafael — confirmed. Quick status:
- us-east1 has spare capacity across two pools; we can absorb up to ~35% of BlueCove steady QPS without impacting other tenants if we limit to read-only model variants.
- There is a routing governance guard that requires a 1-hour notification for cross-region rehomes above 15% per-account. Given P0, I can approve an emergency override but will need a written exec sign-off (recorded in the incident log).

Operational ask for the bridge:
- Approve emergency cross-region override to start 10% canary now and escalate to 50% after 20 minutes validation.
- Hannah: run cache refill after we divert the canary to reduce cold-miss amplification.

I'll prepare a short exec note for sign-off.

— Vanessa
Senior Director, Dedicated Accounts

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Charlie Nguyen <charlie@bluecove.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 08:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production alert: sustained 5xx + token latency spike in us-west2

On it — inventory and runnable steps below. ETA estimates assume we start canary within 5–10m.

Capacity & risk
- us-east1 pool a/b: ~40% spare headroom. No other urgent drains.
- Consistency: BlueCove uses a session affinity cookie; cross-region shift may expose edge cache staleness for ~3–5 minutes on rare keys.

Staged remediation plan (ops commands omitted for brevity):
1) Route 10% of BlueCove production traffic to us-east1 (10m observation). If error rate falls below 1% and p95 < 300ms, proceed.
2) Trigger KV cache refill (prefix list) in both regions.
3) Bump canary to 50% with rolling health checks; if stable after 20m, continue to 100% drain of us-west2 problem AZ.
4) After stabilization, we will reinstate us-west2 routing to the quantized variant and slowly rebalance.

Estimated RTO: 25–45 minutes for customer-visible reduction; 90–120 minutes for full normalization and verification.

Communication: Rafael, please send the external note to Lisa that includes the RTO and our credit offer. I will post the runbook and link the JIRA.

Hannah
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@bluecove.com>, Charlie Nguyen <charlie@bluecove.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Nov 2028 03:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Production alert: sustained 5xx + token latency spike in us-west2 — next steps

Lisa / Charlie — brief update and actions taken: 

What happened (short):
- At ~07:55 PT 11/17, BlueCove's checkout traffic triggered a traffic amplification pattern that led to a KV cache miss storm and 502 amplification in our us-west2 AZs.

What we did (first 90 minutes):
- Opened incident bridge and ran diagnostics with BlueCove SRE. (Internal: incident-3765)
- Deployed emergency cross-region drain: 10% -> 50% -> 100% to us-east1 following the staged plan; canary showed immediate drop in 5xx and p95 improved from 2.8s -> 220ms during canary.
- Pinned read flows to quantized variants in us-west2 to reduce per-token compute while we rebuild caches.
- Performed targeted KV cache refill and reduced negative TTLs on volatile prefixes.

Current status:
- Traffic is being served from us-east1 and us-west2 with the mixed strategy described above. Error rate today has dropped to ~0.9% for BlueCove and p95 latency is ~260ms. We continue to monitor.

Customer impact / next steps: 
- Expected normalization window: 2 hours for full verification.
- We will follow up with a postmortem and a proposed mitigation plan (rate-limiter tuning and cache pre-warm) by EOD PST.
- As a gesture for SLA impact, we will issue a one-time service credit; operations will follow up with details.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md (internal draft).

We own this and will keep you updated every 30 minutes until full recovery. Please let us know any questions.

— Rafael Mendes
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
